fieldMarks: 11.4-12.6 in; pale brown-gray dove with a narrow black ring on the back of the neck.
Big white patches in the outer tail feathers; tail squared or slightly rounded.
Call a deep, repeated 'kuk-KOOOO-kuk'; also a harsh, mewing nasal note.
behavior: Forages mostly while walking on the ground, in flocks outside the breeding season; eats mainly seeds and waste grain, some berries and insects.
Male display flight: steep climb with noisy wingbeats, then a spiral glide with wings and tail spread.
No regular migration; young birds disperse long distances, driving the species' spread.
habitat: Residential areas and farmland with a mix of trees and open ground; thrives better in small towns than large cities.
range: Introduced: reached the Bahamas in 1974, then Florida, and has since spread west and north across much of North America to Oregon and Washington; the Northeast has only scattered strays.

lookalikes.name: Mourning dove
lookalikes.howToTell: Look for the collared-dove's narrow black neck ring and big white patches in the squared outer tail.
